title: Bad Apples on Rotten Tomatoes: Critics, Crowds, and Gender Bias in Product Ratings
eligible_reason: The 'difference-in-differences' compares female vs male movies (first difference) across crowd vs critic reviewers (second difference); there is no treatment adoption timing. The only policy date is Rotten Tomatoes' introduction of verified reviews (23 May 2019), used for subgroup interactions on a post-May-2019 sample.
design_notes: Eq. (3): Score_im = d1*(FemaleMovie_m x Crowd_i) + lambda*ElapsedTime + phi*ReviewPosition + mu_m + eta_i + psi*ReviewYear + e_im, clustered by movie. Tables 3-6 and appendix tables vary fixed effects (movie, reviewer), outcomes (score, extreme-low-rating indicator, sentiment) and female-movie definitions. Treatment is a time-invariant movie attribute interacted with reviewer type, not a binary switch-on at unit-specific dates; includes time-varying controls and a review-year trend.
estimators_reported: OLS triple-type DiD (female movie x crowd) with movie and reviewer FE
screener_notes: Not eligible: no staggered adoption design. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only. Text file is the CESifo working paper (Oct 2024). Data: IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes ratings (scraped/web-collected), box office and Bechdel data; no data-availability statement in the text.
